newsitem.title: USA: Frigid weather to spread across U.S. Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Frigid weather to spread across U.S. Midwest.

text.p: Frigid weather should blanket the U.S. Midwest through Wednesday and, except for isolated areas that may receive up to two inches of snow, corn and soybean harvest should advance.

"I think with all the cold weather, that will solidify the ground. I don't see the snow being deep enough to impede any harvest equipment," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

Palmerino said low temperatures in the Midwest should range from upper single digits Fahrenheit in the northern areas to low 20s along the Ohio River through Wednesday. Highs should range from mid-20s to upper 30s through the Midwest.

The cold air mass will be concentrated east of a line from Montana to Tennessee, said Fred Gesser, meteorologist with Weather Express Inc. The heaviest snow associated with that cold system will be concentrated near the Great Lakes, but other areas may receive moderate amounts through Wednesday.
"Isolated areas each day will get two to four inches, with traces elsewhere," he said of snowfall through Wednesday.
Warmer weather should return to the Midwest Friday and remain through the weekend, said Gesser. High temperatures should move up to the high 40s and 50s across the belt.
"The trend (next week) is for warmer, drier conditions in the grain areas," he said.
